english: like; such as; a kind of
use: Goes before a noun to compare or give an example; casual mitai na does the same job.
name: like, such as
formation: noun + no you na + noun; plain form + you na + noun

example.romaji: dokoka de atta you na ki ga suru
example.ja: どこかで会ったような気がする
example.english: I feel like I've met you somewhere.

examplePolite.romaji: dokoka de atta you na ki ga shimasu
examplePolite.ja: どこかで会ったような気がします
examplePolite.english: I have a feeling we've met somewhere.

notes: -you na ki ga suru, 'I have a feeling that', is its most common use in speech. Before a verb or adjective it becomes -you ni.

use: A judgment from what you see or know; more formal than mitai, so you hear it in polite speech and on the news.
name: it seems
formation: plain form + you da; noun + no you da; na-adjective + na you da

example.romaji: dare mo inai you da ne

examplePolite.romaji: dare mo inai you desu ne
examplePolite.ja: 誰もいないようですね
examplePolite.english: It seems no one is here.

notes: Casual equivalent: mitai. Compare -sou (looks, from appearance) and rashii (I hear).

use: Pushes back on an assumption; often with kanarazu shimo or itsumo.
name: not necessarily

example.romaji: takai kara oishii to wa kagiranai yo
example.ja: 高いからおいしいとは限らないよ

examplePolite.romaji: takai kara oishii to wa kagirimasen yo
examplePolite.ja: 高いからおいしいとは限りませんよ
examplePolite.english: Just because it's expensive doesn't mean it's good.

notes: Kagiru alone means 'nothing beats': 'natsu wa biiru ni kagiru' (nothing beats beer in summer).

use: A confident guess from evidence; stronger than hazu.
name: must be
formation: plain form + ni chigai nai (noun or na-adjective drops da)

example.romaji: ano futari, tsukiatteru ni chigai nai yo
example.ja: あの二人、付き合ってるに違いないよ

examplePolite.romaji: ano futari wa tsukiatte iru ni chigai arimasen
examplePolite.ja: あの二人は付き合っているに違いありません
examplePolite.english: Those two are surely going out.

notes: A little bookish; in chat 'kitto ... da yo' or '... ni kimatteru' (it's obviously) are more common.

english: if; supposing; if it's true that
use: For a pure hypothetical or something you just learned; often moshi ... to shitara.
name: supposing

example.romaji: moshi takarakuji atatta to shitara, nani suru?
example.ja: もし宝くじ当たったとしたら、何する？
example.english: Say you won the lottery, what would you do?

examplePolite.romaji: moshi takarakuji ni atatta to shitara, nani o shimasu ka
examplePolite.ja: もし宝くじに当たったとしたら、何をしますか
examplePolite.english: Supposing you won the lottery, what would you do?

notes: To sureba and to suru to mean the same. 'da to shitara' = if that's the case.

english: I hope; it would be good if
use: Mostly -to ii ne to wish someone well, or -to ii na for your own hope.
name: I hope

examplePolite.romaji: ashita hareru to ii desu ne
examplePolite.ja: 明日晴れるといいですね

notes: Same idea as -tara ii na. As advice it means 'it's best to': 'kono kusuri nomu to ii yo'.

english: as long as; as far as
use: Sets a condition or limit: 'as long as I'm here', 'as far as I know'.
name: as long as / as far as

example.romaji: watashi no shitteru kagiri, kare wa dokushin da yo
example.ja: 私の知ってる限り、彼は独身だよ
example.english: As far as I know, he's single.

examplePolite.romaji: watashi no shitte iru kagiri, kare wa dokushin desu
examplePolite.ja: 私の知っている限り、彼は独身です
examplePolite.english: As far as I know, he isn't married.

notes: 'dekiru kagiri' = as much as possible. 'kyou kagiri' = today only, on sale signs.

use: After a noun it means 'it's up to'; after a -masu stem, 'as soon as', a polite promise at work.
name: depends on / as soon as

example.romaji: iku ka dou ka wa tenki shidai da ne
example.ja: 行くかどうかは天気次第だね
example.english: Whether we go depends on the weather.

examplePolite.romaji: iku ka dou ka wa tenki shidai desu ne
examplePolite.ja: 行くかどうかは天気次第ですね
examplePolite.english: Whether we go will depend on the weather.

notes: 'anata shidai' = it's up to you. 'wakari shidai gorenraku shimasu' (I'll contact you as soon as I know) is a set business line.

english: as long as there's; all you need is
use: Says one thing is all it takes; the general shape is X sae + a -ba form, and areba is the common one.
name: as long as there's

example.ja: スマホさえあれば大丈夫
example.english: As long as I've got my phone, I'm fine.

examplePolite.ja: スマホさえあれば大丈夫です
examplePolite.english: As long as I have my phone, I'll be fine.

notes: 'kimi sae yokereba' = if it's okay with you. Don't mix with de sae, 'even'.

use: Criticises someone for acting against what they are or know; sounds accusing, so keep it out of polite talk.
name: even though (critical)
formation: plain form + kuse ni; noun + no kuse ni; na-adjective + na kuse ni

example.romaji: nani mo shiranai kuse ni, erasou ni iu na yo
example.ja: 何も知らないくせに、偉そうに言うなよ
example.english: You don't know a thing, so quit acting like an expert.

notes: -noni is the neutral 'even though'. Ending a sentence on kuse ni is a jab: 'shiranai kuse ni' (like you'd know).

use: Almost always followed by a negative or a complaint: 'just because X doesn't mean Y'.
name: just because

example.romaji: yasui kara tte, kaisugi da yo
example.ja: 安いからって、買いすぎだよ
example.english: Just because it's cheap doesn't mean you buy that much.

examplePolite.romaji: yasui kara to itte, kaisugi desu yo
examplePolite.ja: 安いからといって、買いすぎですよ
examplePolite.english: Even if it's cheap, that's too much to buy.

notes: Kara to itte is the fuller, more polite form. Compare kara koso, 'precisely because'.

use: Grants one point, then adds a reservation: 'even allowing for that'.
name: even allowing for
formation: noun or plain form + ni shite mo

example.romaji: isogashii ni shite mo, renraku gurai shite yo
example.ja: 忙しいにしても、連絡ぐらいしてよ
example.english: Even if you're busy, at least get in touch.

examplePolite.romaji: isogashii ni shite mo, renraku gurai shite kudasai yo
examplePolite.ja: 忙しいにしても、連絡ぐらいしてくださいよ
examplePolite.english: Busy or not, please at least let me know.

notes: 'sore ni shite mo' = even so, still: 'sore ni shite mo samui ne'. Compare -ni shite wa, 'for a'.

use: Says something is surprising given what it is: 'pretty good for a beginner'.
name: for a
formation: noun or plain form + ni shite wa

example.romaji: shoshinsha ni shite wa umai ne
example.ja: 初心者にしてはうまいね

examplePolite.romaji: shoshinsha ni shite wa jouzu desu ne
examplePolite.ja: 初心者にしては上手ですね
examplePolite.english: You're very good for a beginner.

notes: The result always goes against what you'd expect. Don't mix with -ni shite mo, 'even if'.

english: although; that said; though it's only
use: Plays down what you just said: 'I cook, though it's just simple stuff'.
name: although (playing down)
formation: noun or plain form + to itte mo

example.romaji: ryokou to itte mo, ippaku dake da yo
example.ja: 旅行といっても、一泊だけだよ
example.english: It's a trip, but only one night.

examplePolite.romaji: ryokou to itte mo, ippaku dake desu yo
examplePolite.ja: 旅行といっても、一泊だけですよ
examplePolite.english: I say a trip, but it's only one night.

notes: Casual: 'tte itte mo'. 'nan to itte mo' = when all's said and done.
